walkthroughs.body_html:
Photography — a core area of A-Level Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Photography brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Photography.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which photographer coined the phrase 'decisive moment'?
options: Robert Capa
Henri Cartier-Bresson
Don McCullin
Diane Arbus

mcqs.q: Which setting most directly controls depth of field?
options: ISO
Shutter speed
Aperture
White balance

mcqs.q: What is the significance of Duchamp's 'Fountain'?
options: It challenged the definition of art - the artist's choice, not their skill, becomes the artwork.
He painted indoor scenes.
It demonstrated his sculpting ability.
It is a study of plumbing.

mcqs.q: Why is preserving white in watercolour important?
options: You can simply paint white over other colours later.
It is a study of plumbing.
White comes from the paper showing through - there is no true white pigment in traditional watercolour.
Because white is the most expensive colour.

mcqs.q: What did Pollock mean by his drip paintings being 'in the painting'?
options: He painted indoor scenes.
He literally fell into wet paint.
It is a study of plumbing.
He worked from all sides, making the act of painting central to the meaning.
